messages.content:
As-salamu alaykum. In the Hanafi school of jurisprudence (*Madhhab*), the ruling on music is characterized by caution and a general prohibition of musical instruments. This position is based on the interpretations of the Quran and the Sunnah by the early scholars of Kufa and the foundational imams of the school.

Here is a detailed breakdown of the Hanafi ruling:

### 1. The General Prohibition
The majority of Hanafi jurists consider the use of musical instruments (*ma'azif*) and listening to them to be **Haram** (prohibited) or **Makruh Tahrimi** (prohibitively disliked, which is close to Haram in practice).

This includes stringed instruments (like violins or guitars), wind instruments (like flutes), and most types of drums.

### 2. Evidence from the Quran
Hanafi scholars frequently cite Surah Luqman, Verse 6:
> *"And of mankind is he who purchases idle talk (Lahw al-Hadith) to mislead (men) from the Path of Allah..."* (31:6).

The great Sahabi **Abdullah ibn Mas’ud** (may Allah be pleased with him), whose legal school became the foundation for the Hanafi Madhhab, famously swore by Allah that "idle talk" in this verse refers to singing and music.

### 3. Evidence from the Hadith
The Hanafi position is strongly supported by several Hadiths, most notably a narration in **Sahih Bukhari**:
> The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: *"There will be people from my Ummah who will seek to make lawful: zina (adultery), silk, alcohol, and musical instruments (ma'azif)."*

Hanafi jurists argue that by grouping musical instruments with major sins like adultery and alcohol, the Prophet (peace be upon him) indicated their prohibition.

### 4. Exceptions: The Duff (Tambourine)
The Hanafi school allows a limited exception for the **Duff** (a one-sided drum without rattles or bells). 
*   **When:** It is permitted primarily for weddings (*Nikah*) and Eid celebrations to announce the joy.
*   **Condition:** The lyrics must be wholesome and not contain any impermissible content. Some scholars within the school specify that this is mainly for women and children.

### 5. Singing Without Instruments (Vocal Music)
Regarding singing with the voice alone (without instruments):
*   **Permissible:** If the lyrics are "Hamd" (praise of Allah), "Naat" (praise of the Prophet), or encourage virtue, and it is not done in a way that mimics the style of sinful people (*fasiq*).
*   **Prohibited:** If the lyrics contain themes of passion, indecency, or anything contrary to Islamic belief. If the singing is accompanied by swaying or encourages base desires, it is considered disliked or prohibited.

### 6. Summary of the Hanafi Position
The classical Hanafi texts (such as *Al-Hidayah* and *Fatawa Hindiyya*) emphasize that:
1.  **Listening to music** for entertainment is considered a sin that diminishes one's spiritual state and legal testimony (*adalah*).
2.  **The Goal** of this prohibition is to protect the heart from "Nifaq" (hypocrisy). Imam Abu Hanifa is reported to have said that music "grows hypocrisy in the heart just as water grows grass."

### Compassionate Advice
While the Hanafi ruling is strict on this matter, the intention behind it is to encourage the believer to find peace and tranquility in the **Dhikr** (remembrance) of Allah and the recitation of the **Quran**. 

If you find it difficult to move away from music, scholars suggest replacing it with beautiful Quranic recitations or Nasheeds (vocals only) that remind you of Allah and His Messenger (peace be upon him). May Allah make your journey toward what pleases Him easy and full of reward.

**Allah knows best.**

And Allah knows best.

messages.content: who will come in the last days?

As-salamu alaykum. In Islamic eschatology, the "last days" (Akhir az-Zaman) are marked by several significant figures and groups whose appearances are considered major signs of the Day of Judgment (Yawm al-Qiyamah).

According to the Quran and the authentic Hadith of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), here are the key figures who will appear:

### 1. Imam Al-Mahdi (The Guided One)
The first major figure to appear will be Al-Mahdi. He is a leader from the lineage of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) through his daughter Fatima.
*   **His Role:** He will emerge at a time when the world is filled with injustice and oppression. He will unite the Muslim Ummah and establish justice, peace, and equity on earth.
*   **Description:** The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: *"The world will not come to an end until the Arabs are ruled by a man from my family whose name will be the same as mine and whose father’s name will be the same as my father’s"* (Sunan Abi Dawud).

### 2. Al-Masih ad-Dajjal (The False Messiah / Antichrist)
Following the appearance of the Mahdi, the greatest trial for humanity will emerge.
*   **His Role:** He is a deceiver who will claim to be God. He will be given supernatural powers (by Allah’s permission) to test the faith of people, such as commanding the rain to fall or bringing a semblance of the dead back to life.
*   **Description:** The Prophet (peace be upon him) described him as being blind in one eye (the right eye), looking like a floating grape, with the Arabic letters *Kaf-Fa-Ra* (meaning Kafir/Disbeliever) written between his eyes, which every true believer will be able to read.

### 3. Prophet ‘Isa (Jesus), Son of Maryam
At the height of the Dajjal’s fitnah (tribulation), Prophet ‘Isa (peace be upon him) will descend from the heavens.
*   **His Role:** He will descend at the white minaret in the east of Damascus, resting his hands on the wings of two angels. He will join forces with Imam Mahdi, find the Dajjal at the gate of Ludd (in modern-day Palestine), and kill him.
*   **His Rule:** He will rule the world with justice according to the Sharia (law) of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). During his time, wealth will be so abundant that no one will accept charity, and there will be total peace—even among animals.
*   **Quranic Reference:** *"And indeed, Jesus will be [a sign for] knowledge of the Hour..."* (Surah Az-Zukhruf, 43:61).

### 4. Ya’juj and Ma’juj (Gog and Magog)
During the reign of Prophet ‘Isa, a massive group of people known as Ya’juj and Ma’juj will be released.
*   **Their Role:** They are currently trapped behind a barrier built by Dhul-Qarnayn (as mentioned in Surah Al-Kahf). When they break through, they will swarm the earth in massive numbers, consuming all water and spreading corruption.
*   **Their End:** Prophet ‘Isa and the believers will pray to Allah, and Allah will send a type of worm that will infect their necks, causing them to perish simultaneously.

### 5. The Beast of the Earth (Dabbat al-Ard)
As the very final signs approach, a creature will emerge from the earth.
*   **Role:** The Beast will speak to people and distinguish the believers from the disbelievers, marking their faces so that their spiritual state becomes visible to all.
*   **Quranic Reference:** *"And when the word befalls them, We will bring forth for them a creature from the earth speaking to them..."* (Surah An-Naml, 27:82).

### Summary for the Believer
While these signs are a fundamental part of Islamic belief, the Prophet (peace be upon him) taught that the most important thing is not simply knowing *who* will come, but preparing our own souls for the meeting with Allah.

When a man once asked the Prophet (peace be upon him), "When is the Hour?" The Prophet replied, **"What have you prepared for it?"** (Sahih Bukhari).

**Compassionate Note:** These events can seem overwhelming, but in Islamic tradition, they are shared to provide hope and guidance. They remind us that ultimately, truth will prevail over falsehood, and justice will prevail over oppression. As a believer, the best preparation is to remain steadfast in prayer, seek knowledge, and perform acts of kindness.

And Allah knows best.

3495eb56-572a-4f3e-b5b1-b79e6d399082.name: What are the five pillars of Islam?

messages.content: What are the five pillars of Islam?

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

The Five Pillars of Islam are the core foundations of a Muslim’s life and faith. They are based on a famous teaching of the Prophet Muhammad (peace and blessings be upon him), who said:

> *"Islam is built upon five [pillars]: testifying that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, establishing prayer, giving Zakat, Hajj (pilgrimage) to the House (Ka'bah), and fasting in Ramadan."* (Sahih Bukhari and Sahih Muslim)

Here is a brief explanation of each pillar:

### 1. Shahada (The Testimony of Faith)
This is the most fundamental pillar. It is the declaration: *"Ash-hadu alla ilaha illallah, wa ash-hadu anna Muhammadan rasulullah"* (I bear witness that there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah). Sincere belief in this statement is what enters a person into the fold of Islam.

### 2. Salah (The Five Daily Prayers)
Muslims perform five obligatory prayers throughout the day: Fajr (dawn), Dhuhr (noon), Asr (afternoon), Maghrib (sunset), and Isha (night). Prayer serves as a direct connection between the believer and Allah, providing spiritual strength, peace, and reminders of one's purpose.

### 3. Zakat (Obligatory Charity)
Zakat is a form of social justice and purification of wealth. Muslims who meet a certain threshold of savings (known as *Nisab*) are required to give 2.5% of their surplus wealth annually to those in need, such as the poor, the orphans, and the wayfarers.

### 4. Sawm (Fasting during Ramadan)
Every year during the holy month of Ramadan, healthy adult Muslims abstain from food, drink, and marital relations from dawn until sunset. Fasting is not just about hunger; it is a time for self-discipline, increased devotion, and empathy for those who are less fortunate.

### 5. Hajj (The Pilgrimage to Makkah)
Hajj is the pilgrimage to the Ka'bah in Makkah, Saudi Arabia. It is mandatory once in a lifetime for every Muslim who is physically and financially able to undertake the journey. It is a profound demonstration of the unity of the Muslim Ummah (community), as people from every corner of the world gather in equality before God.

These pillars provide the framework for a life of worship, morality, and service to humanity. May Allah grant us the strength to fulfill these obligations with sincerity and love.

And Allah knows best.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

In Islamic eschatology, **Al-Masih ad-Dajjal** (The False Messiah or the Antichrist) is a major figure who will appear toward the end of time, before the Day of Judgment. His appearance is considered one of the "Greater Signs" of the Hour. The word *Dajjal* comes from the Arabic root *dajala*, which means "to deceive" or "to cover," reflecting his role as the ultimate deceiver.

According to the teachings of the Prophet Muhammad (peace and blessings be upon him), here is a summary of who the Dajjal is and what his arrival entails:

### 1. His Physical Characteristics
The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) described the Dajjal in detail so that the believers would recognize him and not be deceived. Some of these traits mentioned in authentic Hadith include:
*   **The Eye:** He is blind in one eye. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: *"He is one-eyed, and your Lord is not one-eyed"* (Sahih Bukhari). His right eye will look like a floating grape.
*   **The Mark:** The Arabic letters *Kaf-Fa-Ra* (forming the word *Kafir*, meaning disbeliever) will be written between his eyes. Every true believer, whether literate or illiterate, will be able to read it.
*   **Physical Stature:** He is described as being a young man with a ruddy complexion, a large frame, and thick, curly hair.

### 2. His Mission and Deception
The Dajjal will emerge at a time of great hardship and religious negligence. He will travel the entire world at great speed, claiming first to be a prophet and then claiming to be God. 

Allah will allow him to perform miraculous feats as a **trial (fitna)** for humanity:
*   He will have the ability to command the sky to rain and the earth to produce crops.
*   He will have with him what appears to be a "Paradise" and a "Hell," but the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) warned that his paradise is actually fire, and his fire is cool, refreshing water.
*   He will offer wealth and food to those who follow him, while those who reject him will suffer hardship and loss of property.

### 3. Where He Cannot Go
The Dajjal will enter every city on earth except for **Makkah and Madinah**. These two holy cities will be guarded by angels standing in rows, preventing him from entering.

### 4. How to Protect Oneself
The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) taught us several ways to seek protection from this great trial:
*   **Surah Al-Kahf:** Reciting and memorizing the first ten (or last ten) verses of Surah Al-Kahf provides protection against the Dajjal’s deception.
*   **Supplication (Dua):** We are encouraged to seek refuge in Allah from the "Trial of the Dajjal" at the end of every prayer (during the final Tashahhud) before the Taslim.
*   **Fleeing from him:** Believers are advised not to go out to meet him out of curiosity or overconfidence in their faith, but to stay away from him.

### 5. The End of the Dajjal
The Dajjal’s reign will last for forty days: one day like a year, one day like a month, one day like a week, and the rest like normal days. His end will come at the hands of **Prophet Isa (Jesus)**, peace be upon him, who will descend from the heavens. Prophet Isa will pursue the Dajjal and kill him at the gate of Lud (in present-day Palestine/Israel), signaling the end of his deception and the beginning of a period of peace and justice on earth.

### Spiritual Lesson
The mention of the Dajjal serves as a reminder for believers to strengthen their faith (*Iman*), hold fast to the Quran and Sunnah, and not be swayed by worldly illusions. It emphasizes that true sight is not with the physical eyes, but with the heart that recognizes the truth of Allah.

And Allah knows best.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

**Jannah** (Paradise) is the eternal home of peace, joy, and splendor that Allah (SWT) has prepared for His righteous servants in the Afterlife. It is a reward beyond human imagination, where there is no pain, no sorrow, no aging, and no death.

The Prophet Muhammad (peace and blessings be upon him) relayed a Hadith Qudsi in which Allah says:
> *"I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and what has never occurred to the human heart."* (Sahih Bukhari)

Here is a glimpse of Jannah based on the Quran and Sunnah:

### 1. The Gates and Levels of Jannah
Jannah is not just one place, but many levels and degrees of excellence based on a person’s faith and deeds.
*   **The Gates:** There are eight gates of Jannah. One is called *Ar-Rayyan*, reserved exclusively for those who fasted frequently.
*   **The Levels:** There are many levels; the highest and most central part of Jannah is **Jannat al-Firdaws**, located directly under the Throne of Allah.
*   **The Width:** Allah describes Jannah as having a width *“as wide as the heavens and the earth”* (Quran 3:133).

### 2. The Physical Beauty and Environment
The Quran describes Jannah as a lush garden with flowing rivers and eternal shade:
*   **Rivers:** There are rivers of pure water, rivers of milk of which the taste never changes, rivers of wine (delicious and non-intoxicating), and rivers of cleared honey (Quran 47:15). One famous river is *Al-Kawthar*, granted to the Prophet Muhammad (peace and blessings be upon him).
*   **Palaces:** The buildings are made of bricks of gold and silver, with mortar of fragrant musk and pebbles of pearls and rubies.
*   **Climate:** There is no extreme heat or cold; the climate is always perfect and comfortable.

### 3. The Life of the Dwellers
Those who enter Jannah will experience a complete transformation:
*   **Eternal Youth:** Everyone will enter Jannah at the age of 33, the age of strength and vigor, and they will never age.
*   **No Hardship:** There is no need for sleep, no illness, no bathroom needs (impurities will leave the body as a fragrant musk-scented sweat), and no toil or exhaustion.
*   **Perfect Peace:** There is no hatred, jealousy, or ill-will between people. The Quran says: *"And We will remove whatever is in their breasts of resentment"* (Quran 7:43).
*   **Food and Drink:** Whatever food or fruit a person desires will be brought to them instantly. They will eat for pure pleasure, not out of hunger.

### 4. The Spiritual Joys
While the physical rewards are immense, the spiritual rewards are even greater:
*   **Company:** Believers will be reunited with their righteous family members and will have the honor of being in the company of the Prophets and the Sahaba (companions).
*   **The Ultimate Reward:** The greatest joy in Jannah—surpassing all others—is when Allah removes the veil and allows the believers to look upon His Countenance. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said that when the believers see their Lord, they will forget every other pleasure they were given.

### 5. How to Attain Jannah
The Quran repeatedly emphasizes that Jannah is earned through **Iman** (faith) and **Amal Salih** (righteous deeds). It is not just a hope, but a destination we work toward by:
*   Following the commands of Allah and His Messenger.
*   Maintaining the five daily prayers.
*   Having good character and showing kindness to others.
*   Seeking Allah’s forgiveness and mercy.

**A Beautiful Reminder:**
Jannah is a place where every "No" you said to a temptation in this world is replaced with an eternal "Yes." It is the true home for which we were created.

May Allah (SWT) make us among the dwellers of Jannat al-Firdaws and grant us the companionship of the Prophet Muhammad (peace and blessings be upon him) there. Ameen.

And Allah knows best.
